rows.source: Met Office National Severe Weather Warning Service
rows.verified: Met Office warning coverage includes rain, thunderstorms, wind, snow, lightning, ice, extreme heat and fog.

rows.source: Met Office National Severe Weather Warning Service
rows.verified: Users can select a location to review relevant local warnings.

rows.source: Met Office National Severe Weather Warning Service
rows.verified: The warning service is known as the National Severe Weather Warning Service.

rows.source: Met Office National Severe Weather Warning Service
rows.verified: Warnings communicate both forecast weather and the impacts that weather could cause.

rows.source: Met Office National Severe Weather Warning Service
rows.verified: Warnings are intended for people, businesses, emergency responders and government.

rows.source: Met Office National Severe Weather Warning Service
rows.verified: A warning decision depends on expected impacts, not only the meteorological value.

rows.source: Met Office National Severe Weather Warning Service
rows.verified: Warning information supports preparation and action to reduce disruption and harm.

rows.source: Met Office National Severe Weather Warning Service
rows.verified: Current warning information should be checked for the relevant place and period.

rows.source: Met Office National Severe Weather Warning Service
rows.verified: Weather-warning meaning depends on the hazard, colour, likelihood, impact, geography and valid time shown in the current notice.

rows.source: Met Office National Severe Weather Warning Service
rows.verified: A warning area does not prove exact damage, injury or service interruption at an individual parcel.
